title: Lily and the Sun's Secret Colors
markdown:
The sun was painting the meadow gold, like a warm hug for the sleepy flowers. Lily, who loved to build and fix, was watering her little moon-blossoms. They opened their petals slowly at night, like little sleepy yawns. Beside her, Squeaky the squirrel wiggled her nose, which shook like a tiny shaker. She watched a little red beetle climb a tall green blade of grass. Old Mr. Tortoise, with his shell full of sunny stories, blinked slowly, enjoying the warm afternoon.

Suddenly Lily turned on her watering can, and a fine mist sprayed out. Tiny sparkly drops danced in the air. As they caught the sun, little flashes of red, yellow, and blue flickered, like shy butterflies, before they vanished.

Lily’s eyes grew wide and round. Her mouth made a little O. “Oh my!” she whispered. “Squeaky, Mr. Tortoise, did you see that? A little flash of colour!”

Squeaky scampered closer, her bright eyes watching everything. Her bushy tail gave a happy little flick. “Pretty colours!” she chirped, hopping up and down. “Like little flying jewels!”

Mr. Tortoise ambled over, his old eyes wise and calm. “Indeed, Lily,” he rumbled, voice like soft pebbles rolling. “A most peculiar and pretty thing. But how does it happen, I wonder?”

Lily tapped her chin. She remembered learning that light could play tricks when it went through water. “Hmm,” she thought. “Maybe these tiny drops are playing with the sunlight?”

She turned the watering can on again, making a bigger mist this time. A cloud of sparkling water hung in the air. And then a big bright stripe of colours shimmered across the sky. Squeaky, with her super-sharp eyes, pointed a tiny paw. “Look! Look!” she squeaked. “The sunlight goes into the water drops, and then… pop! All the colours come out!”

Lily smiled, a big happy smile. “You’re right, Squeaky!” she said. “The sunlight is shining into the water drops, and the drops are splitting the light into all its secret colours! It’s like the water is showing us what colours are hiding inside the sunshine!”

Mr. Tortoise nodded his wise old head. “That is called refraction, my friends,” he said gently. “When light goes from the air into a water drop, it bends. And each colour in the sunlight bends a little differently. Red bends one way, blue bends another, and all the colours in between bend their own special ways. That’s why we see this beautiful rainbow.”

He paused, letting the wonder of it all sink in. “This is how big rainbows appear in the sky after a rain, when raindrops catch the sun just right. Each drop is like a tiny window, showing us the colours.”

Lily and Squeaky looked at the shimmering colours, their faces bright with awe. Then they looked up at the big blue sky, imagining rainbows everywhere.

“Refraction!” Lily whispered, her heart full of wonder.

Squeaky wiggled her nose, her little mind buzzing. “I wonder,” she chirped, “what other secrets are hiding? Maybe how seeds know which way to grow!”

And as the sun began to set, painting the sky in soft hues, the meadow seemed to hum with the quiet joy of discovering something new. Even a watering can and a bit of sun could hold an enchanting story, if they just took the time to look.
characters: Lily (a moon-blossom waterer), Squeaky (a nose-wiggling squirrel), Tortoise (a sunny-story elder)
author: StoryGen Community
